facts.raw_span: 4-week history of watery diarrhea (20 episodes per day)
vomiting
diffuse abdominal pain aggravated by spicy foods
8-kg weight loss (≈15% of body weight)
brownish macules on the hands and feet
hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk
onychodystrophy
mild hypoproteinemia and hypoalbuminemia (total protein 3.52 g/dL [normal 6.6–8.3], albumin 2.09 g/dL [3.5–5.2])
zinc deficiency (51 µg/dL [70–120])
low vitamin B12 (<150 pg/mL [300–900])
multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa
numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss, along with the presence of Yamada polyps and colon polyps, are consistent with Crohn's disease.
The patient's symptoms of diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss, along with the presence of hypoproteinemia and hypoalbuminemia, are consistent with celiac disease.
The patient's symptoms of skin lesions and onychodystrophy, along with the presence of gastrointestinal polyps, are consistent with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
The patient's laboratory results show a zinc deficiency, which is consistent with a diagnosis of zinc deficiency.
The patient's laboratory results show a low vitamin B12 level, which is consistent with a diagnosis of vitamin B12 deficiency.
The patient's endoscopy results show multiple gastrointestinal polyps, which is consistent with a diagnosis of gastrointestinal polyposis.

rationales.F01: Watery diarrhea is a common symptom of Crohn's disease and gastrointestinal polyposis.
rationales.F04: Significant weight loss is a red flag for Crohn's disease and gastrointestinal polyposis.
rationales.F05: Brownish macules on the hands and feet are more typical of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
rationales.F07: Onychodystrophy can be associated with zinc deficiency.
rationales.F11: Yamada polyps are characteristic of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and gastrointestinal polyposis.
rationales.F12: Numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps are characteristic of gastrointestinal polyposis and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
